newsitem.title: USA: IMCO sees improvements continuing in 2nd half '97.
newsitem.headline: IMCO sees improvements continuing in 2nd half '97.

text.p: IMCO Recycling Inc said Wednesday it expects improvements in processing volume and gross profit per pound to continue in the second half of 1997.

IMCO, the world's largest aluminum recycler that also processes zinc and magnesium, made the forecast as it reported second quarter 1997 net earnings of $3.6 million or $0.28 per common share, 37 percent above net earnings of $2.6 million or $0.21 per share in the same quarter last year.
The company said processing volume in the second quarter totaled 490 million pounds, 32 percent higher than the 372 million pounds processed in the 1996 quarter.
Don Ingram, chairman and chief executive officer, said the company's net earnings and processing volume in the period were higher than in any previous quarter.
"IMCO is beginning to realize the strong earnings potential created by earlier acquisitions and expansions that have sharply increased our capacity," he said.
In the second quarter, the company experienced strong customer demand for aluminum recycling services, and volume rose by 32 percent, he said.
Gross profit per pound rose from both the second quarter of 1996 and this year's first quarter because of the higher volume and better plant operating efficiency, he said.
"We expect these improvements to continue in the second half," he said.
The company said volume in the first six months of 1997 was 922 million pounds, 25 percent above the 739 million pounds processed in the 1996 period.
